notes: KNOWN FAILING — irrlicht's hermes adapter recognizes exactly ONE turn-end signal: Watcher.turnIsDone returns true only for role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop' (watcher.go:426-436), mirrored by parser.go:93-95 which rewrites the event to turn_done on the same equality. Hermes' own vocabulary is wider — 'stop','tool_calls','length','content_filter' (agent/transports/types.py:106) plus 'incomplete' on the codex_responses path — and it persists the abnormal value VERBATIM into messages.finish_reason (conversation_loop.py:2663-2665 → chat_completion_helpers.py:1315-1320 → hermes_state.py:6651-6665). So an aborted turn leaves a real, machine-readable trace in the store and the daemon discards it: the session stays `working` for the rest of the process's life. Nothing rescues it — there is no inactivity sweep on `working` (PR #106 removed the stale-tool timer) and this adapter deliberately declares no IdleFlush seam, precisely because it trusted the explicit boundary. This spec asserts the CORRECT arc, not the bug: the aborted turn must settle back to ready. Trigger: the run caps the model's output (HERMES_MAX_TOKENS / model.max_tokens, cli.py:4206-4217 → agent_init.py:1996-2019), so the essay prompt terminates with finish_reason='length' after hermes' 4 continuation attempts give up (conversation_loop.py:2709-2718). The recipe opens with a throwaway baseline turn because the driver's wait_turn counts only 'stop' rows and resolve_session_id — the sole writer of the staging contract's session.uuid — runs only inside wait_turn; the aborted turn is then covered by a trailing sleep, since wait_turn could never see it. Hermes carries a Process matcher, so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession while the real sessions row is INSERTed only on the first user message — session_birth is anchored to start UNPINNED so the presession cannot steal identity, and every later phase chains via same_session_as. The final settle carries max_delay_ms on purpose: tearing tmux down can close the hermes session (ended_at → the watcher's justEnded terminal), and a teardown-induced ready must NOT be allowed to satisfy the phase and mask the bug. Clear known_failing and re-record once turnIsDone accepts the abnormal terminal finish_reasons the way the sibling opencode watcher already does. `model` is deliberately NOT pinned — the recording home's config.yaml is provisioned at record time.

text: The hermes session appears in ready. Unpinned: the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message (~2s after it), not at launch, and a transient proc-<PID> presession may appear first.
The throwaway baseline prompt drives the session ready → working. This turn exists so the driver can resolve the session id; the scenario's subject is the turn after it.
The baseline turn completes normally — its newest assistant row carries finish_reason='stop', so turnIsDone fires and the session settles back to ready on the SAME session.
The essay prompt drives the session ready → working again: message_count grows while the newest row is not assistant/finish_reason='stop', so the activity event is non-terminal.

THE ASSERTION THIS CELL IS ABOUT (currently failing): the capped turn ends abnormally — hermes gives up after 4 continuation attempts and the newest active row is an assistant row whose finish_reason is not 'stop' — and the session must return to ready promptly, not stick in working. Bounded by max_delay_ms so a ready produced by the teardown's session close cannot satisfy it.
